{"id":"ENG-2207","uuid":"a2130265-5031-4e82-a581-30ef0fa7851e","title":"Add shared node type format resolver to `@repo/utils`","description":"## Problem

* Node type schemas can store `format` at `literal_content.format` or the legacy `literal_content.source_data.format`.
* Roam and Obsidian implement this precedence separately, so their import behavior can diverge while legacy schemas remain.

## Solution

* Add an `@repo/utils` function that reads `literal_content.format` first and falls back to `literal_content.source_data.format`.
* Replace the app-specific precedence logic in the affected Roam and Obsidian import paths.

## Done When

* Unit tests cover the top-level value, legacy fallback, conflicting values, and missing values.
* Roam and Obsidian use the shared resolver, and the top-level value wins when both exist.

## Out of Scope

* Changing schema writers, migrating existing rows, or removing the legacy fallback.
* Client-version enforcement or a general metadata migration framework.

## Notes

* Builds on [ENG-2158](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2158/publish-node-type-format-with-schemas>).
* Agreed in the [August 28 sync meeting](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Toww-3UYl>), with related context in <pull-request id="47c454db-a748-4b37-a9df-dce1a52716c7" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2156-decorate-imported-node-titles-in-roam-from-core-title-9992bc14a074">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1331</pull-request>.","projectMilestone":{"id":"4bbba6d9-e697-45b4-96c7-e3e4638720a4","name":"Architecture Refactors"},"priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2207/add-shared-node-type-format-resolver-to-repoutils","gitBranchName":"eng-2207-add-shared-node-type-format-resolver-to-repoutils","createdAt":"2026-08-31T04:06:47.844Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-15T18:09:43.398Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Database","Publish & Import","Inter-Graph","Obsidian plugin","Roam plugin"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"fdc1ad3c-14d6-4579-bb14-e8e5b1b212c5","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-31T04:06:47.844Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Michael Gartner","createdById":"9ef754d2-efb6-40b1-abbf-38a6b57aeeeb","project":"Post-V0 Roam–Obsidian sync architecture","projectId":"42055007-b7e8-47c3-95a1-8929908034b6","team":"Engineering","teamId":"e69757b7-976a-4567-836f-16f8a4d59df2","relations":{"blocks":[],"blockedBy":[],"relatedTo":[{"id":"ENG-2156","title":"Decorate imported node titles in Roam from `core_title`"},{"id":"ENG-2157","title":"Decorate imported node titles in Obsidian from `core_title`"},{"id":"ENG-2158","title":"Publish node type `format` with schemas"},{"id":"ENG-2208","title":"Publish Obsidian node type format at `literal_content.format`"}],"duplicateOf":null}}

Proposed breakdown, seven tests across five subtasks.

Fixtures gate everything. Three shapes: local, upload, read. The upload shape and the read shape differ, so one fixture cannot serve as both. Read fixtures carry their `file_references` rows even though this ticket asserts nothing about them, so the asset tickets extend the same fixtures rather than building a parallel set. The unasserted rows are deliberate.

`crossAppNodeContract.example.ts` must be corrected before it can seed fixtures. Its Roam half does not match what `roamToCrossAppConverters.ts` emits, on four points: `direct.value` holds the stripped title where the converter writes the full page title, `full.contentType` is `markdown` where the converter writes `roamMarkdown`, `full.value` is a `#` heading plus prose where `buildFullMarkdown` emits bullet lines and no title, and `scale: "document"` and both `localId` fields are missing. Its Obsidian half is correct on the title and has not been checked against the Obsidian publish path.

Subtasks:

1. Correct the example fixture, then build the fixtures. Gates the rest.
2. Publish tests, 2, vitest. Roam local to upload, Obsidian local to upload. Each asserts `direct`, `full`, schema metadata, and source identity (`localId`, `rid`).
3. Fetch tests into Roam, 2, vitest. Roam-shaped and Obsidian-shaped read fixtures. Each runs the import twice and asserts no duplicate.
4. Fetch tests into Obsidian, 2, vitest. Same assertions. Budget most of this subtask for mock machinery rather than for the tests. `importSelectedNodes` is already exported, so exporting helpers does not help: it calls `getLoggedInClient` and `getSupabaseContext`, constructs a `QueryEngine`, and the per-node body below it drives the vault throughout, through `getFileByPath`, `read`, `adapter.exists`, `createFolder`, `process` and `fileManager.renameFile`. Writing a note into a vault is what this code does, so a vault fake is unavoidable and is the bulk of the work.
   * Note: A small(ish) part of it will become unnecessary when we refactor Obsidian to use the CrossApp contract, which would make the transformation assertions (title, body, schema metadata, source identity) testable as pure data. But the vault fake itself survives that refactor, so it is worth building well.
   * Note: We are considering extracting the per-node body of `importNodes` into its own function as part of the test harness, a pure refactoring, so the test drives one node rather than the space-grouping loop above it.
     * The extraction would expose seams that invite design improvements, which are a separate scope. Example: `existingFile` is currently looked up inside the loop, from `importedFiles` then `queryEngine.findExistingImportedFile`. Passing it in as a parameter instead would make the duplicate-prevention contract explicit and let the test assert create versus update directly.
5. Bridge test, 1, cucumber. Loads both upload fixtures, reads them back through the shared-node query, asserts the read fixtures. The only test that checks the upload and read shapes agree. Runs with the suite that wipes the database.

Subtasks 2 and 3 can start as soon as 1 lands. `apps/roam` already has harnesses to extend for both (`publishNodesToGroups.test.ts`, `materializeSharedNode.test.ts`, `importSharedNodes.test.ts`). Obsidian's publish side needs no new scaffolding either, since `findEmbeddedAttachments` and `syncPublishedNodeAssets` are exported.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-09-23T16:05:50.468Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-23T16:05:50.416Z","parentId":"4b0e658c-cd01-44b1-a653-68c28608ffc9","resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"4b0e658c-cd01-44b1-a653-68c28608ffc9","body":"@michaelgartner looking at this ticket, and I think it needs tighter scoping, and that some of the scoping belongs post-v0. 
What I think we'd want:
The basic success paths where a node is published in either platform, and imported in either platform. We would mock the database, so really we'd have publish Roam→upload, publish Obsidian→upload, fetch Roam-shaped→Roam, fetch Roam-shaped→Obsidian, fetch Obsidian-shaped → Roam, fetch Obsidian-shaped → Obsidian. The shape of upload and download is not exactly the same, so I'd add a cucumber test to make sure that they don't drift.
Problem: No vitest in Obsidian. Easy enough to add, but clearly a separate task. Do we want to do it?
Note: Do we want all of this for Friday? It's currently blocking the parent task, which would be otherwise closed. I think we may want to detach this.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-09-17T16:49:05.801Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-17T17:29:35.820Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"1119dae1-b8aa-406b-8759-580042e74893","body":"We'll also want to revisit after we refactor ImportNode in Roam, and all of Obsidian, to use CrossRef.

I notice ENG-2045 actually depends on ENG-2091, so it's not independent. And ENG-1985 seems to build the database-to-CrossAppNode converter that ENG-2091 relies on, even though its own description is stale and doesn't mention this explicitly.

Looking at the other tickets, ENG-1878 depends on several likely-completed tickets and is blocked on a post-V0 project, while ENG-1879 is deferred until Obsidian and Roam align on shared contract code, tying it to the ENG-2413 decision. The format tickets ENG-2209, 2207, 2208 were agreed on in a late-August meeting and still need verification against main.

For the remaining Architecture Decision tickets, I'm weighing whether to pull full comment histories or instead query the Linear GraphQL API directly to filter for comments whose body starts with "Decision," which would be much more efficient than scanning every comment thread.

Three of the seven tickets already reference Architecture Decisions work (ENG-2045 waits on ENG-2091, ENG-1985 was re-scoped by it, ENG-1879 was deferred). Next I'll pull just the `Decision:` comments from the Architecture Decisions milestone instead of loading full discussion threads.

I'm also considering whether this change actually alters observable behavior: if Roam's node schema writer sets both the top-level format and source_data.format to the same value, nothing changes, and the only edge case is when they diverge — which seems rare enough that no demo video is warranted for the Roam side.

{"id":"ENG-2061","title":"Refactor `RoamFullContentNode` to use `CrossAppNode` contract","description":"## Problem

* `RoamFullContentNode` and `CrossAppNode` describe the same node. Michael: "It is basically the same type, different name" ([type](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-740e5638ca02078f61f320b8654a1a5b2cad3350046a466abd1f8bf556c95b95L11>)).
  * `RoamFullContentNode` (`convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts`) is a flat datalog row: snake_case fields, times typed `string | number`, and `text`, `format` and `node_title`.
  * `CrossAppNode` is nested, with `content.direct` and `content.full`.
* Michael: "This likely removes the need for this converter" ([converter](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-3369b2954fe17df153f37f163d9fb033a7afd3063bf9e77142aed5ff214e805aR5>)). The converter, `fullContentNodeToCrossApp` (`roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`), derives `coreTitle` from the title format and builds the full content. That work moves; it doesn't go away.

## Solution

* Remove `RoamFullContentNode`. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s Done When includes this ticket.

**Open decisions**

1. Is this the first sub-ticket of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>, part of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s single change, or closed because `RoamFullContentNode` is a fair input row type?
2. Does the full-content producer, `getSharedRoamNodesWithFullContentUpdatesSince`, return `CrossAppNode` directly? <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> removed the type but deferred "Producers returning CrossAppNode directly".
3. Does this ticket also cover `RoamDiscourseNodeData` (`getAllDiscourseNodesSince.ts`), the row type the direct-content path uses? No ticket covers it.

## Done When

* `RoamFullContentNode` is gone from the Roam codebase, including tests.

## Out of Scope

* Changing the sync write calls (<issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>).

## Notes

* Current state: the type is used in `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`, `roamToCrossAppConverters.ts` and `__tests__/syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts`. PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> deletes `convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts` and types the times as `number`.
* History:
  * 2026-07-22 meeting: Marc-Antoine: "Suggestion: A converter for each roam-based type to CrossAppType, in a separate file." {"id":"ENG-1823","title":"Use the unified upsert_concepts in Obsidian","description":"## Problem

* Obsidian sync writes Concepts and Content in separate calls, to `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`. If one call fails, we have partially defined nodes in the database.
* `upsert_concepts` accepts Content embedded in each Concept since <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue>, so one call can write the full node.

## Solution

* Remove the call to `upsert_content`. Send each node with its Content in a single call.

**Open decisions**

1. {"id":"ENG-1824","title":"Use the unified upsert_concepts in Roam","description":"## Problem

* Roam sync writes Concepts and Content in separate calls, to `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`. If one call fails, we have partially defined nodes in the database.
* It would be better to send the full node, with Content as sub-objects of the Concept, in a single upsert. `upsert_concepts` accepts this since <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue>.
* Roam publish already writes in a single call. Roam sync does not.

## Solution

* Remove the calls to `upsert_content`. Unify the Content computations to create the CrossAppNode type, and send it, after conversion, in a single call.

**Open decisions**

1. Does the single call go through the upsert route (<issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>) or straight to `upsert_concepts`? Confirming that in `discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept`, since only certain fields are destructured, `format` ends up nested inside `source_data` rather than at the top level — this bug is still present on main. I'm now tracing the three write paths at lines 55, 94, and 180, where 55 handles node schema and 94 handles relations.

Checking the reader side: Obsidian's `parseSchemaLiteralContent` falls back from `source_data.format` to `obj.format`, so it still works correctly even with the nested format, confirming ENG-2208 is independent of ENG-2207. I'm also considering that rows published before ENG-2208 will retain the old `source_data` structure, unlike Roam rows which get backfilled via ENG-2175.

For ENG-2207 testing, packages/utils lacks a test runner, so I need to decide whether to add vitest there (which touches the lockfile) or place tests somewhere vitest already exists, like packages/database's test setup — this feels like a decision to flag with a proposed default rather than just deciding unilaterally. The resolver logic itself (top-level format wins, falling back to empty string) seems solid.

Turning to the ticket's requirement to replace precedence logic in Roam and Obsidian import paths — Roam's covered, so now I need to check whether apps/obsidian depends on @repo/utils for its parseSchemaLiteralContent function. I'm also considering whether this change actually alters observable behavior: if Roam's node schema writer sets both the top-level format and source_data.format to the same value, nothing changes, and the only edge case is when they diverge — which seems rare enough that no demo video is warranted for the Roam side.

For ENG-2209, I'm checking who actually calls dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp — if nothing currently reads the format field from this converter, relocating it is safe, since Roam's resolveSharedNodeTypes queries the DB directly rather than going through this converter. That makes ENG-2209 a self-contained data-layer change with no existing consumers, so it doesn't need its own video either. But I'm now weighing whether this converter should fall back to source_data.format for Obsidian-origin rows per the ENG-2158 pattern, since the ticket's scope notes this fallback behavior explicitly.

The ticket marks that fallback out of scope, meaning Obsidian-origin rows would leave format undefined in the CrossAppNodeSchema output even though it's actually sitting in metadata — which seems acceptable since that's what the spec calls for. Still, given that ENG-2207 already introduces a resolver for this exact fallback, it feels natural that 2209 could reuse it, and I'm debating whether to flag this as a gap, especially since this converter is likely meant for future importers in the CrossApp migration work where Obsidian rows would need that fallback to get a format at all.

ENG-2045 depends on ENG-2091 per the decision, so it's not independently startable. For ENG-1985, the node converter doesn't exist on main yet, and the ticket description seems stale with a dormant draft PR from Marc-Antoine; its output fields also hinge on ENG-2091's open question about adding spaceUri and other db ids to CrossAppNode, plus ENG-1879 oddly being a child of it.

I'm wondering whether the node converter could just ship with base fields while ENG-2091 layers in extras later, though the "Done When" criteria would need rewriting regardless — I want to check what's actually in PR #1184's diff before deciding. Meanwhile ENG-1878 looks vague too, though the example contract file does exist and Marc-Antoine left a comment on ENG-1879 about it.

Now I'm tracing the dependency chain: the Roam side has four errors needing fixes before seeding fixtures, Michael wants ENG-1879 deferred until Obsidian and Roam share contract code (after ENG-2165/1986), and ENG-1878's own blockers are already resolved even though it blocks several Icebox tickets downstream. The ENG-1866 decision notes that ENG-1863's fixtures never landed and would only resurface as a regression test, which reinforces how stale and underspecified these MVP0-era problem statements and "Done When" criteria really are.

Marc-Antoine's proposed breakdown starts with fixtures first, but since Michael wants these deferred until the contract code aligns, they aren't actually "clear and ready" — they haven't gone through decision review and still depend on ENG-2165/ENG-1986. That's a problem because Architecture Refactors' own entry criteria require that nothing a ticket depends on be undecided, yet ENG-1879 explicitly hinges on the still-pending Obsidian/Roam alignment work.

Checking the Architecture Decisions tickets awaiting Michael/Marc-Antoine's review: ENG-2061 removes RoamFullContentNode as the first step toward ENG-2165, with a decision scoping it strictly to what PR #1333 did; ENG-1824 depends on ENG-2061 finishing first, so it isn't independent; ENG-1823 looks more self-contained with a single upsert_concepts call and documented scope notes. I want to read through the actual descriptions of ENG-1823, ENG-1824, and ENG-2061 to confirm they've been properly updated.

ENG-2425, 2426, and 2427 are still Ticket Drafts awaiting human approval before moving to Backlog, so they sit outside the Architecture Refactors milestone — 2427 implements the ENG-2394 decision for Obsidian, while 2425/2426 are Roam bugs. Since the user's focus is specifically on Architecture Refactors and decided issues, I'll just note these drafts separately as still awaiting review. Tallying up the seven Architecture Refactors tickets, it looks like ENG-2209, ENG-2208, and ENG-2207 are ready and independent once their descriptions get a refresh, since the resolver already exists and what's left is mostly Obsidian-side work.

The rest aren't ready: ENG-2045 is blocked on ENG-2091's open question for Marc-Antoine, ENG-1985 has a stale description and a stale draft PR also dependent on that same open question, and ENG-1878/1879 are vague MVP0-era tickets Michael deferred until both apps share contract code, with 1879 depending on 1878. Looking at the Architecture Decisions that are approved to build but still waiting on Michael or Marc-Antoine to review them, I see ENG-2061 feeding into ENG-1824 (Roam) sequentially and ENG-1823 (Obsidian) independently, plus ENG-2091 still open and ENG-1986 further out.

Checking independence among ENG-2207, 2208, and 2209: they each touch different files with no overlap, and since the Obsidian reader already falls back to top-level parsing, ENG-2208 doesn't actually need ENG-2207 done first — though I want to double check that interplay between ENG-2208 and the Obsidian reader more carefully.

After ENG-2208, Obsidian writes format into literal_content while source_data omits it, but both the Obsidian and Roam readers correctly fall back to the top-level format field, so resolution still works. The edge case is whether an older released Obsidian client that only reads source_data.format would break here.

That's probably out of scope since it's a client-version enforcement issue rather than a schema one. I should still check whether otherData flows into other fields like importedFromRid, and verify there aren't other write paths in the Obsidian node schema around conceptConversion or other schema writers. Neither ENG-2209 nor ENG-2208 seem to touch Roam's UI directly—they're database converter and Obsidian-only writer changes—but I want to flag any possible Roam-observable side effects before concluding.

Per the demo-handoff guidance, pure-logic PRs don't need videos since passing unit tests suffice, so ENG-2209 and ENG-2207 are covered there. ENG-2208 changes what Obsidian writes to the database, and any live proof would involve the Obsidian side rather than Roam's product surface, so none of these three tickets appear to require a Roam-facing demo video.

For the sync refactor pair, ENG-2061 is a pure internal cleanup with no visible effect, while ENG-1824 changes the sync write path in a way that's behavior-affecting but not UI-visible — so the right proof there is probably a DB readback after sync runs rather than a product video. I should double-check a couple more details before finalizing, starting with the Obsidian concept conversion logic.

I also still want to verify whether other schema writers behave similarly, whether apps/obsidian depends on @repo/utils, and read through the descriptions for ENG-2061, ENG-1823, and ENG-1824 since those fall under the decided Architecture Refactors the user asked about. I'll check PR #1184's diff stats too, to see if it includes a node converter, though the Roam node schema writer's top-level format isn't something I need to dig into further.

ENG-2208 is still unresolved on main due to the `format`/`source_data` mismatch, ENG-2045 is blocked on ENG-2091 as expected, and ENG-1985 has no node converter yet with PR #1184 stale since 7/10. Next I'll check other Obsidian schema writers, whether Obsidian can import `@repo/utils`, PR #1184's contents, and the three approved Architecture Decision tickets.

{"id":"ENG-2061","title":"Refactor `RoamFullContentNode` to use `CrossAppNode` contract","description":"## Problem

* `RoamFullContentNode` and `CrossAppNode` describe the same node. Michael: "It is basically the same type, different name" ([type](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-740e5638ca02078f61f320b8654a1a5b2cad3350046a466abd1f8bf556c95b95L11>)).
  * `RoamFullContentNode` (`convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts`) is a flat datalog row: snake_case fields, times typed `string | number`, and `text`, `format` and `node_title`.
  * `CrossAppNode` is nested, with `content.direct` and `content.full`.
* Michael: "This likely removes the need for this converter" ([converter](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-3369b2954fe17df153f37f163d9fb033a7afd3063bf9e77142aed5ff214e805aR5>)). The converter, `fullContentNodeToCrossApp` (`roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`), derives `coreTitle` from the title format and builds the full content. That work moves; it doesn't go away.

## Solution

* Remove `RoamFullContentNode`. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s Done When includes this ticket.

**Open decisions**

1. content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/sid/.claude-company/skills/decision-review

# Decision review

Turns a milestone of open decision tickets into tickets sid and the team can decide from,
top-down:

1. **milestone**: group the tickets that share a decision under parent tickets, and link the
   groups by dependency. Runs once per milestone.
2. **group**: review one group in depth, link its tickets, and rewrite them so a reader gets
   the issue, the discussion history and the open decisions. Runs once per group.
3. **decide**: record each decision on its ticket.

**Read the state before choosing steps.** Every step has a "Skip when" condition. Read the
state from Linear first, tell sid in one line which steps you'll run and which you'll skip,
then run them. Don't skip a step on judgment. On 2026-10-16 two steps were skipped that way:
the groups were never checked against the descriptions, and a lean was posted unchecked.

**Analysis goes in the chat, never in a file.** Name groups by their ticket IDs, never by a
code like "A1". Write to sid's Roam home page (`propose_write` to Sid/Home) only when sid asks.
Linear changes are the point of the process; each one waits for sid's approval as described
below.

Scripts: `S=/home/sid/.claude-company/skills/decision-review/scripts`. They are `roam.mts`
(Roam full-text and tree reads; the discourse-graph MCP only searches titles) and
`token-usage.py`.

sid asked for Roam history as part of this review, so the "don't read Roam to fill a spec
gap" rule doesn't apply inside this skill. Still never read
`Worklog/Push and pull nodes between Roam and Obsidian` whole.

The ENG-2091 pilot (2026-10-16), done inline, cost about 3.2M tokens for one ticket. One
agent per group, tiers and a fresh context per group bring that to about 1M per ticket or less.

## milestone <name>

### 1. Survey (main context, about 0.1–0.3M)

Skip when: every open ticket in the milestone is a group parent, sits under one, or was
already surveyed and left standing alone, and no open ticket was created after the newest
group parent. Otherwise survey only the tickets that fail this check.

1. Run `list_issues` for the project with
   `fields: [id, title, status, projectMilestone, parentId, labels, createdAt]`, and keep the
   milestone's open tickets.
2. Read the scope sources once, and keep every fact that settles a question: the project
   description; for product decisions, also P-DIS-166 (UCs and Non-Goals), P-ENG-185, and
   P-ENG-170 for group access.
3. Draft groups from the titles.
4. Confirm them by reading every ticket's description, Done When and existing links
   (`get_issue` with relations). Look at code only where a ticket names a file or path.
   Titles alone mislead: on 2026-10-16, ENG-2005 and ENG-1866 were grouped by title as
   "contract validation", but the descriptions show ENG-2005 is input validation for the
   upsert route and ENG-1866 is a one-off check of Obsidian's relation export.
5. Make a group only where two or more tickets share one decision: parent and children, the
   same code path, or the same UI surface. A ticket that shares no decision stands alone.
6. Note the links between groups that the ticket text states, such as one ticket naming
   another's work.
7. Tier each group and estimate its review cost (see Tiers).
8. Post in the chat:
   - the scope facts
   - one row per group: ticket IDs with titles, the shared decision in one line, tier,
     estimate
   - the standalone tickets
   - the links between groups, the run order (groups that unblock others first) and the total

   Wait for sid to approve the groups.

### 2. Structure in Linear (main context)

Skip when: every approved group has a parent ticket and the links between groups exist.

- Each group gets a parent ticket, created with
  `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.agents/skills/dg-create-engineering-ticket/SKILL.md`
  (the repo copy; the `.claude` copy may be stale): Ticket Draft, `Created by Claude`, in the
  milestone. Show the drafts in the chat first.
- In a parent's description, name tickets by ID and never write a count ("six tickets"), so
  a ticket moving between groups doesn't leave the parent wrong.
- Set each ticket's parent. Sub-issues can nest: a ticket that already has a parent goes
  under the group parent and keeps its children. FEE tickets can sit under an ENG parent.
- A real dependency becomes `blocks`, between parents and between tickets. A link that only
  informs a decision becomes `related`.
- Give sid the drags for the order (see Linear facts).

## group <parent ticket id>

One group per run, in the run order. Before an agent runs, post one line: which steps run,
the tier and the estimate. No agent runs before sid has seen the estimate.

### 1. Read the group (main context)

Never skip; it's cheap.

- Read the parent and every sub-issue: description, comments, links and linked PRs. Note
  which sub-issues are already prepared (they have **Open decisions** and a **History**) and
  whether they changed since (new comments, edits, PR activity).
- If a ticket doesn't share the group's decision, propose moving it before anything else.
- Read the prepared tickets of the groups that block this one. They're the earlier review the
  agent builds on. If a sub-issue was reviewed in an earlier chat but never prepared (for
  example the ENG-2091 pilot), ask sid to paste that review.

### 2. Deep review (one fresh subagent)

Skip when: every sub-issue is prepared and none changed since.

- Launch `Agent` with `subagent_type: general-purpose`, `model: opus` and the brief below.
  Run one at a time by default, and never more than two at once
  (see [[feedback-no-extra-usage]]).
- The agent returns the full review as its final message. Its report is not shown to sid, so
  the main context posts it in the chat after step 3.

### 3. Check the review (main context)

Runs whenever step 2 ran.

- Spot-check one code claim and one history claim: open the cited file:line, rerun
  `roam.mts text <uid>`, and read `roam.mts context <uid>` before trusting what a block is
  said to mean. Fix or flag anything wrong.
- Check every lean against the review's own History and the scope facts. The lean is a
  judgment call, so it stays with the main context.
  - A lean that drops a direction the team recorded must name that direction and say what
    outweighs it.
  - Stale PRs, merge conflicts and unanswered review threads describe the state of the work.
    They are not reasons to drop a direction.
  - Rewrite or flag any lean the history contradicts before it reaches sid. (FEE-890,
    2026-10-16: the agent leaned "close" against the route the team agreed on 2026-07-17, and
    the main context posted it unchecked.)
- If a group with open decisions blocks this one, write each lean as conditional on those
  answers.
- Post the review, ending with its dependency map and its real token cost next to the
  estimate. Measure the cost with `python3 $S/token-usage.py <agent output file>`. The token
  count in the agent's completion notice is its final context size, not its cost.

### 4. Links inside the group (main context)

Skip when: the dependency map adds nothing to the links already in Linear.

- Propose the new `blocks` and `related` links in the chat, and add them after sid agrees.
- Don't add a link whose kind depends on an open decision, such as whether one ticket
  duplicates another. Add it once that's decided.

### 5. Prepare the tickets (main context)

Skip for a ticket that is already prepared and unchanged.

Makes each ticket ready to decide, before anyone decides it. A person reading the ticket
should get the issue, the thread of discussion and the open decisions, clearly and simply.

1. Sort the tickets so the one that unblocks the most comes first.
2. Draft each ticket with `dg-engineering-writing-style`, in the five template headings:
   - Problem: the issue in plain words.
   - Solution: what's agreed, then **Open decisions** as a numbered list of questions.
   - Notes: current state (PRs, call sites), then a dated **History** with the person and a
     link (Roam uid or PR comment).
   - Keep the existing text that is still true, mostly word for word. Mark done work as done
     instead of deleting it.
3. Verify every quote, date and author against its source before showing the drafts.
4. Show all drafts in the chat, in order, each with a one-line "What changed".
5. After sid approves, re-read each ticket and confirm nobody edited it since you read it,
   then save. Add no `Decision:` comment at this stage.
6. If the parent's description no longer matches its sub-issues, fix it too.

## decide <ticket ids>

For each ticket sid decides:
1. Change only what the decision settles, with `dg-engineering-writing-style`, and show sid
   the draft in the chat.
2. After sid approves, update Linear and add a top-level `Decision:` comment that links the
   history.
3. Move a ticket to another milestone only when sid says so. If a decision moves a ticket
   between groups, update both parents' descriptions.

## Linear facts

- Linear adds a `related` link for every ticket a description mentions.
- Linear keeps one link per pair of tickets: adding `blocks` replaces an existing `related`.
- The manual order can't be set from here: the MCP has no sort order field, and
  `LINEAR_API_KEY` is read-only. Give sid the drags, in dependency order; the view's Ordering
  must be Manual.
- Description history keeps every earlier version (issue menu, Show description history).
- Property changes in the first 3 minutes after a ticket is created don't appear in its
  activity log. Changes made through the MCP appear under sid's name.

## Tiers

- **deep**: architecture or cross-app behavior, where history matters (2–3M)
- **medium**: one feature, with some history (about 1.5M)
- **light**: a small UX change; one Roam search, no digging (about 0.7M)

## Agent brief

Fill the `<>` slots, and paste the scope facts from the survey.

```
You are reviewing Linear decision tickets for sid, the project lead. Read-only: do not edit
code, Linear or Roam, and do not write files.
Tickets: <ids and titles>. Milestone: <Architecture|Product> Decisions. Tier: <deep|medium|light>.
Scope facts already settled: <from the survey>
Earlier review to reuse, not redo: <the prepared tickets of blocking groups, by ID, and any
pasted review, or none>. Read prepared tickets in Linear; their Open decisions and History
are the earlier review.
Overlapping open tickets outside this group: <ids and titles, or none>. Read their title and
description only, to cite overlaps; don't review them.

Return your review as your final message, in markdown, with one section per ticket answering
in this order:
1. Is the problem clear? Quote the claim. Mark the parts that are stale (already shipped),
   ambiguous or guessed.
2. Is it still a problem? Check against origin/main (`git fetch -q origin main`, then
   `git grep ... origin/main` or `git show origin/main:<path>`) and cite file:line. For a
   product ticket, say what the code does today and whether a user has hit it (FEE tickets,
   Roam PAI/RES/FLO nodes, pilot notes).
3. Is the context there? Look for missing links to overlapping tickets, an unstated design
   question, or a Done When nobody can test.
4. History: dated, attributed, and written by people only. Sources: the ticket's comments,
   the PR review threads (`gh api repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pulls/<n>/comments`)
   and Roam full text (commands below). For meeting notes, attribute positions by the speaker
   labels and say who typed the block. Skip lines marked BOT. Give each item its Roam uid or
   PR link. Before saying what a block means, read its parent with `roam.mts context <uid>`.
5. Should it be rewritten with the engineering writing skill? Yes or no, with a one-line
   reason. Don't write the rewrite.
6. Options: first the ones on record in the history, then at most two of your own. Name each
   option with a short descriptive phrase, never a letter or code. End with one lean and its
   reason. If the history records a team decision, start from it; a lean that departs from it
   must say what outweighs it.
7. What else: its order relative to other tickets, the decision owner, size and split, and
   the next action.
For a light-tier ticket: answer 1, 2, 3 and 5 in full, 4 from a single search, and 6 and 7 in
one line each.

End with a "Dependencies" section: a small tree of what blocks what, then what only informs a
decision, duplicates, tickets that are tasks rather than decisions, and any work no ticket
covers.

Linear: load mcp__linear-server__get_issue and list_comments with ToolSearch first.
Roam (run from /mnt/data/projects/dg-team-mcp):
  ./node_modules/.bin/tsx $S/roam.mts search [--page "<title>"] <term>...  case-sensitive, so try variants
  ./node_modules/.bin/tsx $S/roam.mts context <uid>[:depth]...             ancestors plus siblings
  ./node_modules/.bin/tsx $S/roam.mts tree <uid> [depth]
  ./node_modules/.bin/tsx $S/roam.mts text <uid>...
The Project page is "Project/Push and pull nodes between Roam and Obsidian"; its meetings sit
under its Meetings block. The dev meeting page is "Sync / Dev team". Never read the Worklog
page whole.

Budget: about <25 deep | 15 medium | 8 light> tool calls for up to three tickets, plus about
5 per extra ticket. Put independent calls in one message, and pipe long output through head
or cut.
```

## Rules

- Never review a group's tickets in the main context. Each ticket adds about 100K of context,
  and every later call re-reads it.
- Report every review's real token cost in the chat. When real numbers drift from the tier
  estimates, update the estimates.
- Real costs so far:
  - Upsert path (ENG-1794, ENG-1823, ENG-1824, FEE-890, FEE-891, ENG-2166), 6 tickets, deep:
    2.0M and 39 tool calls, against an estimate of 2.5M and 30 calls (2026-10-16).
  - CrossApp types (ENG-2091, ENG-2061, ENG-2165, ENG-1986), 4 tickets, deep, ENG-2091 from
    scratch: 2.3M and 38 tool calls, against an estimate of 2.1M and 30 calls (2026-10-16).

{"id":"ENG-2091","title":"Unify SharedNode and CrossAppNode","description":"## Problem

* We have two types that represent an abstraction of a node, `SharedNode` (`packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts`) and `CrossAppNode` (`packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`). This makes for a larger cognitive surface.
  * `SharedNode` is the discovery listing: what a user sees for the nodes in a shared space. It has no content body.
  * `CrossAppNode` is the write payload, with direct and full content.
* There are aspects of SharedNode that are missing from CrossAppNode:
  * ~~reference_content (missing)~~ Done: <issue id="99bbd340-1a9c-43d7-8251-0fecde588a34" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129/populate-reference-content-from-crossappnode-and-roles-from">ENG-2129</issue> added `slots` to both types.
  * sourceId: unclear. `SharedNode.sourceLocalId` already maps to `CrossAppBase.localId`.
  * directMetadata: the direct Content row's `metadata`, not `literal_content`. Only Obsidian reads it, to get `filePath`.
  * Space and listing fields: `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`, `schemaId` and the decorated `title`. Roam discovery and import use them.
* We have a lot of code that started using the SharedNode and will need refactoring: 8 files in `apps/roam/src`, and Obsidian's `getPublishedNodesForGroups` (`importNodes.ts`).

## Solution

* Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes.
* Take the functions that create SharedNodes from database data, and create equivalent functions that create CrossAppNodes instead
  * No such function exists for nodes today. `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` covers schemas and relations only.
* Start using those new functions in the client code
* Remove SharedNodes

**Open decisions**

1. Does discovery return `CrossAppNode`, or do we keep `SharedNode` as a separate listing type? Michael (2026-07-22) and Marc-Antoine (2026-08-03) pointed to `CrossAppNode`. Sid (2026-07-20) described `SharedNode` as a lightweight listing.
2. If discovery returns `CrossAppNode`, do the space and listing fields go into `CrossAppNode`, or into a listing type that wraps it (for example `{ node, space, schemaDbId, directMetadata }`)?
3. What did "sourceId" mean?
   1. Equivalent to sourceLocalId
4. Which ticket builds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` function for nodes: this one or <issue id="0183af0a-6eb6-42b5-a4bd-67ce8d8ed38f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985/define-converters-between-database-schemas-and-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1985</issue>?
5. <issue id="fbc284c7-3cd5-45f8-af76-69797693d685" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2045/remove-obsidian-getpublishednodesforgroups-wrapper-consume-shared">ENG-2045</issue> moves Obsidian onto `SharedNode`. Does it wait for this ticket, or change its target?

## Done When

* We have removed SharedNodes without loss of functionality

## Out of Scope

* Adding functionality, adjacent refactors.

## Notes

* This ticket doesn't depend on the upsert route (<issue id="9153e532-2ad1-4043-b2e7-6ae4edf446f1" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2412/decide-the-upsert-path-for-roam-and-obsidian-writes">ENG-2412</issue>): discovery is a read path.
* History:
  * 2026-07-15 meeting: Michael: "create a task to update `CrossAppNode` and any callers to remove dbId". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/sYQ9O9CJj>) <issue id="46fbb09e-4f2d-4a9b-9a3b-0de4b532ae9e" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2036/remove-ref-from-the-cross-app-node-contract">ENG-2036</issue> (<pull-request id="ce170656-7f6d-4c67-b32e-7a0d511bdc62" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2036-simplify-the-cross-app-node-contract-057a05658547">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1235</pull-request>) did this on 2026-07-16.
  * 2026-07-20: Michael on <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>: "Are we planning on re-using a CrossApp contract for the return type?" [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3611773589>)
  * 2026-07-20: Sid replied: "CrossApp contract is for the setters and getters converters … SharedNode is a lightweight listing of what a user sees for the nodes that are in shared space." He planned the getters for <issue id="8d484b94-3f20-4341-866e-3b95315eaa90" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1856/store-source-identity-metadata-for-roam-imported-nodes">ENG-1856</issue>, which was released on 2026-07-27 without a node getter. [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3613796080>)
  * 2026-07-22: Michael on <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>: "eventually should be CrossAppNode contract, but that can be defered to the next project". [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3632617180>)
  * 2026-08-03: Marc-Antoine created this ticket.
  * 2026-08-07 meeting: Michael: "#decided to add spaceId to CrossAppBase", to materialize `importedFromRid` on import. [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/AU5C3t2lh>) On main, `CrossAppBase` has no `spaceId`. <issue id="297707e9-c42a-42c0-b121-cd7924ea102a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2050/add-rid-optional-in-the-crossapp-base">ENG-2050</issue> (<pull-request id="569f3a6a-c11c-440e-9080-c3fbf8be9e9e" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2050-re-introduce-rid-optional-in-the-crossapp-base-e3bf6bcad804">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1282</pull-request>, 2026-08-19) added an optional `rid`.","status":"Backlog","relations":{"blocks":[],"blockedBy":[],"relatedTo":[{"id":"ENG-2050","title":"Add rid (optional) in the CrossApp base"},{"id":"ENG-1856","title":"Store source identity metadata for Roam imported nodes"},{"id":"ENG-2045","title":"Remove Obsidian getPublishedNodesForGroups wrapper, consume shared SharedNode directly"},{"id":"ENG-1985","title":"Define converters between database schemas and cross-app schemas"},{"id":"ENG-2036","title":"Remove Ref from the cross-app node contract"},{"id":"ENG-2129","title":"Populate `reference_content` from `CrossAppNode` and `roles` from `CrossAppNodeSchema`"},{"id":"ENG-2412","title":"Decide the upsert path for Roam and Obsidian writes"},{"id":"ENG-2416","title":"Research: Test OpenSpec with Milestone 1"},{"id":"ENG-2413","title":"Decide how Roam and Obsidian move onto the CrossApp types"}],"duplicateOf":null}}

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.

=== feedback_stay_in_worktree.md

When the session environment header says `Primary working directory: /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>`, do not `cd` out of that worktree for ANY command — not for lint, not for tsc, not for grep, not for anything.

**Why:** The Bash tool's cwd persists between commands. The moment I run `cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam && npx eslint ...`, every subsequent `Edit` with an absolute path under `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam/...` lands in the main repo on `main`, not the worktree. The Edit tool happily writes the file because the path exists — there is no warning. By the time I notice (often only when the user says "I don't see it in my IDE"), the main branch's working tree has half a PR's worth of uncommitted changes, and the worktree is empty.

This happened once on ENG-1660: 5 files edited in main on branch `main` instead of the worktree. Recovery required `git diff > patch`, `git apply` in worktree, `git restore` in main. Easy to fix but a real risk every time — if the user had run `git add -A && git commit` from main while I was still editing, my changes would land on `main` directly.

**Second failure mode (ENG-1575): a read-only `cd` poisons the build/copy/verify pipeline.** Here the Edits were fine (absolute worktree paths), but I `cd`'d to `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam` for a *harmless-feeling* read-only peek at shared `node_modules` (Blueprint source) and never cd'd back. The next `npm run build`, `npx eslint/tsc`, and `cp dist/.` all inherited main as cwd — so I built `main` (none of the PR's commits), copied that to the test dir, and the "passing" lint/tsc validated main's unedited file. I shipped a wrong build to the user's test dir and reported it as correct. The read-only cd is the sneaky one: it doesn't trip the Edit-path check, so nothing feels wrong until the artifact is already out. **Detection cue:** print `pwd` + `git rev-parse --short HEAD` at the top of any build/check command — if HEAD isn't the worktree branch's tip, cwd has drifted.

**How to apply:**
- Use absolute paths starting with the worktree path: `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>/apps/roam/...`.
- For Bash commands that have a working-directory requirement (lint, prettier, tsc, pnpm scripts), use `git -C <worktree>` or run from the worktree path: `(cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>/apps/roam && npx eslint ...)` so the subshell exits without changing the parent cwd.
- Or use `pushd`/`popd` style: `cd /path/to/worktree/apps/roam && ... && cd -`.
- Before any `Edit` call when working in a worktree session, double-check the path starts with the worktree path, not the main-repo path.
- If you must `cd` (e.g., for `npx` to find the right `package.json`), `cd` only to a subdirectory of the worktree.

**Third failure mode (ENG-2060 pr-video, 2026-08-10): a foreground `cd` to the main checkout wedges the whole shell.** Newer worktree-isolated sessions have a guard that refuses ANY Bash command while the persisted cwd is the shared checkout — including `pwd` and the `cd` back. A foreground `cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/... && npx tsx probe.ts` locked out every subsequent command. **Recovery:** call `EnterWorktree` with `path: <worktree>` — it resets the session cwd to the worktree and everything unblocks. Background (`run_in_background`) commands don't persist cwd, so they're safe for main-checkout-cwd needs; but prefer `( cd ...; cmd )` subshells everywhere.

Cross-ref: [[feedback_pr_scope_discipline]] — a wrong-repo edit silently expands PR scope to "files on main" which is the worst kind of scope creep.
=== feedback_worktree_node_modules_symlink.md

Git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` start with **no `node_modules`** — checks fail with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: @repo/eslint-config` because this is a pnpm workspace and `@repo/*` packages live in per-package `node_modules`.

**Why (updated 2026-07-10, ENG-2019):** Symlinks resolve `@repo/*` workspace packages to the MAIN repo's checkout. That's only correct when the worktree branch leaves `packages/*` untouched. If the branch adds/changes anything in `packages/*`, tsc/eslint see the stale main-repo copy; and MIXED states (some dirs symlinked, some real from a filtered install) are worst of all — one mix broke Roam's global types, another broke Obsidian's React 18/19 peer resolution.

**How to apply:**
- Branch touches only `apps/*` code: symlink root + per-package `node_modules` from the main repo (fast, gitignored, never committed).
- Branch touches `packages/*`: run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the worktree root instead (shared pnpm store, ~5–45s). If a mixed symlink/real state exists, remove the symlinks and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --force` to rebuild the virtual store cleanly.
- Never run `--no-frozen-lockfile` casually: it re-resolves unrelated packages (an @types/node dedup cascaded into React type mixing that broke Obsidian tsc, would have been red CI). To add one dep, hand-add the importer entry to pnpm-lock.yaml reusing an existing catalog resolution (PR #1216 did it in 3 lines), then frozen install.

**Root `pnpm ci:validate` in a symlinked worktree (2026-09-02, ENG-2141):** symlink EVERY workspace that has a package.json, not just the ones you touch. `apps/tldraw-sync-worker/node_modules` was missing and turbo failed fast on its `check-types`, skipping every other task. Separately, the main checkout's virtual-store hoist `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@types/react` was a July link to React 18 types while packages/ui needs 19, so `@repo/ui check-types` failed locally even though `.pnpm/lock.yaml` matched the lockfile and CI at the same commit was green. That is a main-checkout environment problem (a fresh frozen install there), not something to fix from a worktree. Fallback proof when it bites: `pnpm exec turbo run test:unit` at the worktree root plus per-app `tsc`, and cite the green CI run at the base SHA.

**Husky rewrites the shared hooks path (2026-09-25):** `pnpm install` in a worktree runs the root `prepare` script (`husky`), which sets the repo-wide `core.hooksPath` to relative `.husky/_`. The main checkout's value is absolute `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.husky/_` (the Entire hook wrappers live there). After any worktree install, check `git config core.hooksPath` and restore the absolute value if it changed.

See [[feedback_stay_in_worktree]], [[feedback_rename_worktree_branch_before_push]], [[feedback_fix_relocated_lint_warnings]].
=== feedback_rename_worktree_branch_before_push.md

When pushing a branch created by EnterWorktree (auto-named `worktree-<ticket>`), first rename the local branch to the Linear `gitBranchName` (e.g. `eng-1373-drag-and-drop-pages-to-canvas`, dropping the `worktree-` prefix) with `git branch -m <name>`, then push. Do NOT push via a `HEAD:eng-XXXX` refspec to a differently-named remote branch.

**Why:** sid wants the local and remote branch names to match the Linear convention so the PR auto-links to the issue and the branch name is clean.

**How to apply:** after committing in the worktree, `git branch -m <linear-gitBranchName>` then `git push -u origin <linear-gitBranchName>`. See [[feedback_stay_in_worktree]].
=== feedback_independent_pre_pr_review.md

When sid says "use the pre-pr-review skill before PR", run `/home/sid/.claude/commands/pre-pr-review.md` as its own read-only pass (a fresh Opus agent per PR, against `gh pr diff N` plus the worktree) after implementation is done, and again after any follow-up commit. The implementing agent saying "I reviewed it" is not the review.

**Why:** On 2026-08-23 sid asked "for each of the pr you did .. did you do the pre-pr-review" for #1330/#1331/#1332; only self-reviews had run. Independent passes then found real defects the implementers missed: a producer key (`author_uid` vs `author_local_id`) that would have blanked `author_id` across the published corpus, a stale legacy-store cache after type creation, and a lossy `{Source}` decoration. See [[project-review-system-v2]].

**How to apply:** Launch the reviewers once the branch is pushed; adjudicate findings yourself (fix in-scope, defer with a note, never rubber-stamp); re-run after fix commits; report per PR what was fixed vs deferred. Don't create Linear tickets for deferrals on sid's behalf — list them for sid to file.

**Re-review mode (added 2026-09-01):** the skill file itself (`/home/sid/.claude/commands/pre-pr-review.md`, "Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)") defines DIFFERENT steps for follow-up pushes: delta only (`git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD`), findings-closure first (fixed/not-fixed/deferred per prior finding and reviewer/bot comment), steps 1–3 on the delta, shrunk step 4, escape hatch if the follow-up adds new surface. When launching the reviewer agent for a follow-up push, don't dictate scope in the launcher prompt (that's what went wrong on ENG-2088, 2026-09-01: the launcher hard-coded full-diff during a re-review) — pass the facts (last-reviewed SHA, what the push answers) and let the reviewer make the mode call via the skill's Mode gate. Per sid (same day): mode choice stays a judgment call, not a black/white rule — a follow-up push can genuinely warrant a full pass (new surface, moved base, doubtful prior coverage), and the reviewer should say which mode it chose and why.
=== feedback_no_git_stash_in_worktrees.md

`refs/stash` is a single ref shared by ALL worktrees of a repository. During the 2026-07-05 six-agent parallel run, two subagents ran `git stash`/`git stash pop` concurrently in sibling worktrees: one popped the other's WIP into its tree and both stashes were ejected/dropped (recovered via dangling commits).

**Why:** stash push/pop in any worktree mutates the same stack; concurrent use is a race. Note the repo's husky/lint-staged pre-commit hook ALSO stashes (backup) on every commit, so even parallel `git commit`s across worktrees can race.

**How to apply:**
- Tell subagents working in parallel worktrees: never use `git stash`; diff against HEAD or copy files to the scratchpad instead.
- Run commits across worktrees sequentially, never in parallel (the pre-commit hook stashes).
- The stash stack holds ~6 old WIP entries from past sessions; don't pop them casually — ownership is unclear.

Related: [[feedback_merge_just_commit]] (never stash mid-merge), [[feedback_worktree_node_modules_symlink]].

=== feedback_stay_in_worktree.md

When the session environment header says `Primary working directory: /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>`, do not `cd` out of that worktree for ANY command — not for lint, not for tsc, not for grep, not for anything.

**Why:** The Bash tool's cwd persists between commands. The moment I run `cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam && npx eslint ...`, every subsequent `Edit` with an absolute path under `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam/...` lands in the main repo on `main`, not the worktree. The Edit tool happily writes the file because the path exists — there is no warning. By the time I notice (often only when the user says "I don't see it in my IDE"), the main branch's working tree has half a PR's worth of uncommitted changes, and the worktree is empty.

This happened once on ENG-1660: 5 files edited in main on branch `main` instead of the worktree. Recovery required `git diff > patch`, `git apply` in worktree, `git restore` in main. Easy to fix but a real risk every time — if the user had run `git add -A && git commit` from main while I was still editing, my changes would land on `main` directly.

**Second failure mode (ENG-1575): a read-only `cd` poisons the build/copy/verify pipeline.** Here the Edits were fine (absolute worktree paths), but I `cd`'d to `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam` for a *harmless-feeling* read-only peek at shared `node_modules` (Blueprint source) and never cd'd back. The next `npm run build`, `npx eslint/tsc`, and `cp dist/.` all inherited main as cwd — so I built `main` (none of the PR's commits), copied that to the test dir, and the "passing" lint/tsc validated main's unedited file. I shipped a wrong build to the user's test dir and reported it as correct. The read-only cd is the sneaky one: it doesn't trip the Edit-path check, so nothing feels wrong until the artifact is already out. **Detection cue:** print `pwd` + `git rev-parse --short HEAD` at the top of any build/check command — if HEAD isn't the worktree branch's tip, cwd has drifted.

**How to apply:**
- Use absolute paths starting with the worktree path: `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>/apps/roam/...`.
- For Bash commands that have a working-directory requirement (lint, prettier, tsc, pnpm scripts), use `git -C <worktree>` or run from the worktree path: `(cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>/apps/roam && npx eslint ...)` so the subshell exits without changing the parent cwd.
- Or use `pushd`/`popd` style: `cd /path/to/worktree/apps/roam && ... && cd -`.

=== feedback_worktree_node_modules_symlink.md

Git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` start with **no `node_modules`** — checks fail with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: @repo/eslint-config` because this is a pnpm workspace and `@repo/*` packages live in per-package `node_modules`.

**Why (updated 2026-07-10, ENG-2019):** Symlinks resolve `@repo/*` workspace packages to the MAIN repo's checkout. That's only correct when the worktree branch leaves `packages/*` untouched. If the branch adds/changes anything in `packages/*`, tsc/eslint see the stale main-repo copy; and MIXED states (some dirs symlinked, some real from a filtered install) are worst of all — one mix broke Roam's global types, another broke Obsidian's React 18/19 peer resolution.

**How to apply:**
- Branch touches only `apps/*` code: symlink root + per-package `node_modules` from the main repo (fast, gitignored, never committed).
- Branch touches `packages/*`: run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the worktree root instead (shared pnpm store, ~5–45s). If a mixed symlink/real state exists, remove the symlinks and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --force` to rebuild the virtual store cleanly.
- Never run `--no-frozen-lockfile` casually: it re-resolves unrelated packages (an @types/node dedup cascaded into React type mixing that broke Obsidian tsc, would have been red CI). To add one dep, hand-add the importer entry to pnpm-lock.yaml reusing an existing catalog resolution (PR #1216 did it in 3 lines), then frozen install.

**Root `pnpm ci:validate` in a symlinked worktree (2026-09-02, ENG-2141):** symlink EVERY workspace that has a package.json, not just the ones you touch. `apps/tldraw-sync-worker/node_modules` was missing and turbo failed fast on its `check-types`, skipping every other task. Separately, the main checkout's virtual-store hoist `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@types/react` was a July link to React 18 types while packages/ui needs 19, so `@repo/ui check-types` failed locally even though `.pnpm/lock.yaml` matched the lockfile and CI at the same commit was green. That is a main-checkout environment problem (a fresh frozen install there), not something to fix from a worktree. Fallback proof when it bites: `pnpm exec turbo run test:unit` at the worktree root plus per-app `tsc`, and cite the green CI run at the base SHA.

**Husky rewrites the shared hooks path (2026-09-25):** `pnpm install` in a worktree runs the root `prepare` script (`husky`), which sets the repo-wide `core.hooksPath` to relative `.husky/_`. The main checkout's value is absolute `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.husky/_` (the Entire hook wrappers live there). After any worktree install, check `git config core.hooksPath` and restore the absolute value if it changed.

Since ENG-2413's group review already surfaced the key decision (discovery returns CrossAppNode) and the open question from Marc-Antoine on ENG-2091, the deep review for these two tickets looks light — ENG-2045's history is tiny and probably doesn't need an agent, while ENG-1985 has a longer thread worth tracing through its creation, draft PR, and follow-up comments about task structure.

I'm weighing whether to just do the deep review inline rather than spin up a subagent, since I've already read most of the relevant history, but the skill explicitly says not to skip steps on judgment — deep review only gets skipped when sub-issues are already prepared and unchanged, which isn't clearly the case here.

Next, ENG-1878 and ENG-1879 need a new parent ticket deciding whether/when to build cross-app fixtures and contract tests. I'm thinking that parent should live in Architecture Decisions even though the sub-tickets currently sit in Architecture Refactors, and I'd propose moving them back so sid can decide — leaning toward building the fixture set and contract tests now.

This cluster feels like medium tier given the September history and the Roam F15 planning context, around 1.5M tokens. I also need to note that ENG-2413 blocks this fixtures/tests parent, since the tests should only land once both apps share the contract code.

Moving ENG-1879 out from under ENG-1985, and running ENG-2413 first since it unblocks everything else. Totaling roughly 2.2M tokens feels steep, so I'm weighing whether to skip the agent for ENG-2413 and prepare it inline from what I already know, presenting that as an alternative path for the user to approve.

But the skill's point about not silently skipping steps was written precisely to prevent this kind of shortcut without visibility. Since presenting the cheaper option explicitly to sid isn't silent skipping, I'll lay out the groups with their standard estimates per the skill, mention the inline alternative briefly, and let sid decide rather than deciding unilaterally.

Reconsidering the grouping itself though: since ENG-1985 and ENG-2045 both share the ENG-2091 decision which already sits in the ENG-2413 group, consistency with the skill's rule means folding them into that group too, with ENG-1985 keeping its own children and ENG-1879 shifting to the new parent.

Before posting, I should verify ENG-2413's and ENG-2091's descriptions to see if they need updating to reflect their sub-issues, and also recheck ENG-1983's status and the ENG-1879 comment thread for context.

My plan for this turn: invoke the decision-review skill covering ENG-2045, ENG-1985, ENG-1878, and ENG-1879, quickly pull the two parent issues, and then gather facts for the orchestrator brief — PR template, adherence skill, worktree list, obsidian test files, and memory files on worktree rules.

I'll invoke the skill first since it loads instructions, and batch the other reads—ENG-2413, ENG-2091, PR template—in parallel since they're independent.

{"id":"ENG-2091","title":"Unify SharedNode and CrossAppNode","description":"## Problem

* We have two types that represent an abstraction of a node, `SharedNode` (`packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts`) and `CrossAppNode` (`packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`). This makes for a larger cognitive surface.
  * `SharedNode` is the discovery listing: what a user sees for the nodes in a shared space. It has no content body.
  * `CrossAppNode` is the write payload, with direct and full content.
* There are aspects of SharedNode that are missing from CrossAppNode:
  * ~~reference_content (missing)~~ Done: <issue id="99bbd340-1a9c-43d7-8251-0fecde588a34" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129/populate-reference-content-from-crossappnode-and-roles-from">ENG-2129</issue> added `slots` to both types.
  * sourceId: unclear. `SharedNode.sourceLocalId` already maps to `CrossAppBase.localId`.
  * directMetadata: the direct Content row's `metadata`, not `literal_content`. Only Obsidian reads it, to get `filePath`.
  * Space and listing fields: `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`, `schemaId` and the decorated `title`. Roam discovery and import use them.
* We have a lot of code that started using the SharedNode and will need refactoring: 8 files in `apps/roam/src`, and Obsidian's `getPublishedNodesForGroups` (`importNodes.ts`).

## Solution

* Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes.
* Take the functions that create SharedNodes from database data, and create equivalent functions that create CrossAppNodes instead
  * No such function exists for nodes today. `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` covers schemas and relations only.
* Start using those new functions in the client code
* Remove SharedNodes

**Open decisions**

1. Does discovery return `CrossAppNode`, or do we keep `SharedNode` as a separate listing type? Michael (2026-07-22) and Marc-Antoine (2026-08-03) pointed to `CrossAppNode`. Sid (2026-07-20) described `SharedNode` as a lightweight listing.
2. If discovery returns `CrossAppNode`, do the space and listing fields go into `CrossAppNode`, or into a listing type that wraps it (for example `{ node, space, schemaDbId, directMetadata }`)?
3. What did "sourceId" mean?
   1. Equivalent to sourceLocalId
4. Which ticket builds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` function for nodes: this one or <issue id="0183af0a-6eb6-42b5-a4bd-67ce8d8ed38f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985/define-converters-between-database-schemas-and-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1985</issue>?

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
