tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

input.title: Add a database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter for nodes
input.description:
## Problem

- ENG-1983 defined the CrossApp types. This ticket covers converting between them and the database.
- Done: the converters from CrossApp types to the database are on main in `crossAppConverters.ts` (ENG-2003, ENG-2004, ENG-2017, ENG-2018). ENG-2146 added the converters from the database to CrossApp types for schemas and relations in `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`.
- Missing: nothing converts database rows to `CrossAppNode`. Discovery builds `SharedNode` by hand instead (`buildSharedNodes` in `sharedNodes.ts`). ENG-2091 needs this converter to return `CrossAppNode` from discovery and remove `SharedNode`.

## Solution

- Add a converter from database rows to `CrossAppNode`, and its bulk form, next to `dbNodeSchemaToCrossApp` in `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`.
- Cover the fields `CrossAppNode` has on main. ENG-2091 adds its new fields to the converter when it adds them to the type.
- Take the rows discovery already reads, with `content.full` optional. `modifiedAt` is the latest `last_modified` of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content, as `lastModified` is today.

**Open decisions**

input.title: Remove Obsidian's getPublishedNodesForGroups wrapper and read CrossAppNode directly
input.description:
## Problem

- Obsidian's `getPublishedNodesForGroups` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:53`) is a thin wrapper over shared discovery. Its only job is remapping `SharedNode` to the local `PublishedNode` type (`:43`):
  - ISO strings (`created` / `lastModified`) → epoch numbers (`createdAt` / `modifiedAt`)
  - `directMetadata` (`Json`) → extracted `filePath: string | undefined`
- Michael on PR #1216: "`getPublishedNodesForGroups` is now redundant. It looks like the only thing it is doing is adding `filePath`, which doesn't warrant an entire wrapped function."
- ENG-2091 replaces `SharedNode` with `CrossAppNode`. It can't remove `SharedNode` while this wrapper, Obsidian's only reader of shared discovery, still uses it.

## Solution

- Remove the `getPublishedNodesForGroups` wrapper and the local `PublishedNode` type. Have `ImportNodesModal` (and the `ImportableNode` conversion path) read `CrossAppNode` directly, moving the `filePath`-from-`directMetadata` extraction to the single call site that needs it.
- Do this as a sub-issue of ENG-2091: after ENG-2091 adds the discovery function that returns `CrossAppNode`, and before it removes `SharedNode`. The wrapper is then deleted once, not rewritten and then deleted.

**Open decisions**

1. The import dialog shows author names by the author's database account id (`ImportNodesModal.tsx:130`, `:371-373`; `typeUtils.ts:92-97`). Does `CrossAppNode` carry that id, or does Obsidian look names up by the account's local id? This is one of the three fields in ENG-2091's open question for Marc-Antoine.

## Done When

- `getPublishedNodesForGroups` and the local `PublishedNode` type are gone.
- Obsidian's import path reads `CrossAppNode` directly.
- A manual import in Obsidian lists the same nodes, titles, dates and author names as before. No automated test covers this path.

## Out of Scope

- Changing discovery itself (ENG-2091).
- Obsidian sync's write path (ENG-1986).

## Notes

- Current state: the wrapper's only caller is `ImportNodesModal.tsx:69`. A comment at `apps/obsidian/src/types.ts:103` still names the wrapper.
- History:
  - 2026-07-20: Michael on PR #1216: "`getPublishedNodesForGroups` is now redundant." [PR comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3611738812) Also: "Are we planning on re-using a CrossApp contract for the return type?" [PR comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3611773589)
  - 2026-07-20: Sid created this ticket to keep PR #1216 a pure extraction, and replied that `SharedNode` is "a lightweight listing of what a user sees for the nodes that are in shared space." [PR comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3613796080)
  - 2026-07-22: Michael on PR #1216: "eventually should be CrossAppNode contract, but that can be defered to the next project". [PR comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3632617180)
  - 2026-10-22: Sid decided this ticket waits for ENG-2091 and reads its type.

{"id":"ENG-2413","uuid":"b90793f4-5dc0-40fc-9942-95895531ba24","title":"Decide how Roam and Obsidian move onto the CrossApp types","description":"## Problem

* These tickets move app code from app-specific node types to the CrossApp types: <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> (SharedNode), <issue id="17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2061/refactor-roamfullcontentnode-to-use-crossappnode-contract">ENG-2061</issue> (RoamFullContentNode), <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> (Roam sync) and <issue id="f1c9f2d5-4eac-47d8-b4a5-a862196ef911" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1986/refactor-obsidian-sync-to-use-the-new-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1986</issue> (Obsidian sync). <issue id="0183af0a-6eb6-42b5-a4bd-67ce8d8ed38f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985/define-converters-between-database-schemas-and-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1985</issue> builds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter for nodes that <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> uses, and <issue id="fbc284c7-3cd5-45f8-af76-69797693d685" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2045/remove-obsidian-getpublishednodesforgroups-wrapper-consume-shared">ENG-2045</issue>, a sub-issue of <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue>, removes Obsidian's discovery wrapper before <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> removes `SharedNode`.
* <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> overlaps <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>, and <issue id="f1c9f2d5-4eac-47d8-b4a5-a862196ef911" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1986/refactor-obsidian-sync-to-use-the-new-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1986</issue> overlaps <issue id="9969e706-c4c9-4405-ad9e-70f888d270b9" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1823/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-obsidian">ENG-1823</issue>. Which tickets carry the sync work depends on the upsert route decision in <issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>.

## Solution

* <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> and <issue id="17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2061/refactor-roamfullcontentnode-to-use-crossappnode-contract">ENG-2061</issue> don't depend on the upsert route and can be decided now. Decide <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> and <issue id="f1c9f2d5-4eac-47d8-b4a5-a862196ef911" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1986/refactor-obsidian-sync-to-use-the-new-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1986</issue> after the upsert path decisions.
* Decide whether <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> and <issue id="f1c9f2d5-4eac-47d8-b4a5-a862196ef911" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1986/refactor-obsidian-sync-to-use-the-new-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1986</issue> block or duplicate <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> and <issue id="9969e706-c4c9-4405-ad9e-70f888d270b9" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1823/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-obsidian">ENG-1823</issue>.
* Record each decision as a `Decision:` comment on its ticket.

## Done When

* Every sub-issue has a `Decision:` comment.
* Every sub-issue is in Architecture Refactors or closed.

## Out of Scope

## Notes

* <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> and <issue id="f1c9f2d5-4eac-47d8-b4a5-a862196ef911" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1986/refactor-obsidian-sync-to-use-the-new-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1986</issue> wait on the upsert path decisions in <issue id="9153e532-2ad1-4043-b2e7-6ae4edf446f1" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2412/decide-the-upsert-path-for-roam-and-obsidian-writes">ENG-2412</issue>.

input.title: Add a database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter for nodes
input.description:
## Problem

- ENG-1983 defined the CrossApp types. This ticket covers converting between them and the database.
- Done: the converters from CrossApp types to the database are on main in `crossAppConverters.ts` (ENG-2003, ENG-2004, ENG-2017, ENG-2018). ENG-2146 added the converters from the database to CrossApp types for schemas and relations in `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`.
- Missing: nothing converts database rows to `CrossAppNode`. Discovery builds `SharedNode` by hand instead (`buildSharedNodes` in `sharedNodes.ts`). ENG-2091 needs this converter to return `CrossAppNode` from discovery and remove `SharedNode`.

## Solution

- Add a converter from database rows to `CrossAppNode`, and its bulk form, next to `dbNodeSchemaToCrossApp` in `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`.
- Cover the fields `CrossAppNode` has on main. ENG-2091 adds its new fields to the converter when it adds them to the type.
- Take the rows discovery already reads, with `content.full` optional. `modifiedAt` is the latest `last_modified` of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content, as `lastModified` is today.

**Open decisions**

1. What does the converter do with a row the contract can't represent, such as one with no author, no created date or no core title? Discovery skips some incomplete rows (`sharedNodes.ts:165-195`) but keeps nodes without an author (`sharedNodes.ts:235`), while `CrossAppNode` requires `authorId`. The schema converter throws instead (`dbToCrossAppConverters.ts:105-108`), and in a listing one throw hides every node.

## Done When

- A converter from database rows to `CrossAppNode` exists in `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`.
- Unit tests cover slots in the same space and across spaces, the latest-of-three `modifiedAt`, and the rule for incomplete rows.

## Out of Scope

- Refactor the existing sync code to use converters.
- Switching discovery and its callers to `CrossAppNode` (ENG-2091).

## Notes

- Draft PR #1184 is obsolete. It targets the ENG-1983 branch and adds converters to the database that main now has in another form, so it can be closed.
- History:
  - 2026-07-01: Marc-Antoine created this ticket. He opened draft PR #1184 on 2026-07-02.
  - 2026-07-06: Michael on this ticket: "We'll break this into sub PR's to handle only the required converters at this time". In that day's meeting notes, right after this ticket, he typed: "let's only introduce new code only when we need it". [Roam](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/q5T9hG7i2)
  - 2026-07-20: Sid planned the database-to-CrossApp getters for ENG-1856 on PR #1216. ENG-1856 was released without a node getter. [PR comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3613796080)
  - 2026-08-21: ENG-2146 (PR #1300, Marc-Antoine) added the converters from the database for schemas and relations.
  - 2026-10-22: Sid decided this ticket builds the converter for nodes, and ENG-2091 uses it.

input.title: Remove Obsidian's getPublishedNodesForGroups wrapper and read CrossAppNode directly
input.description:
## Problem

- Obsidian's `getPublishedNodesForGroups` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:53`) is a thin wrapper over shared discovery. Its only job is remapping `SharedNode` to the local `PublishedNode` type (`:43`):
  - ISO strings (`created` / `lastModified`) → epoch numbers (`createdAt` / `modifiedAt`)
  - `directMetadata` (`Json`) → extracted `filePath: string | undefined`
- Michael on PR #1216: "`getPublishedNodesForGroups` is now redundant. It looks like the only thing it is doing is adding `filePath`, which doesn't warrant an entire wrapped function."
- ENG-2091 replaces `SharedNode` with `CrossAppNode`. It can't remove `SharedNode` while this wrapper, Obsidian's only reader of shared discovery, still uses it.

## Solution

- Remove the `getPublishedNodesForGroups` wrapper and the local `PublishedNode` type. Have `ImportNodesModal` (and the `ImportableNode` conversion path) read `CrossAppNode` directly, moving the `filePath`-from-`directMetadata` extraction to the single call site that needs it.
- Do this as a sub-issue of ENG-2091: after ENG-2091 adds the discovery function that returns `CrossAppNode`, and before it removes `SharedNode`. The wrapper is then deleted once, not rewritten and then deleted.

**Open decisions**

1. The import dialog shows author names by the author's database account id (`ImportNodesModal.tsx:130`, `:371-373`; `typeUtils.ts:92-97`). Does `CrossAppNode` carry that id, or does Obsidian look names up by the account's local id? This is one of the three fields in ENG-2091's open question for Marc-Antoine.

## Done When

- `getPublishedNodesForGroups` and the local `PublishedNode` type are gone.
- Obsidian's import path reads `CrossAppNode` directly.
- A manual import in Obsidian lists the same nodes, titles, dates and author names as before. No automated test covers this path.

## Out of Scope

- Changing discovery itself (ENG-2091).
- Obsidian sync's write path (ENG-1986).

## Notes

- Current state: the wrapper's only caller is `ImportNodesModal.tsx:69`. A comment at `apps/obsidian/src/types.ts:103` still names the wrapper.
- History:
  - 2026-07-20: Michael on PR #1216: "`getPublishedNodesForGroups` is now redundant." [PR comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3611738812) Also: "Are we planning on re-using a CrossApp contract for the return type?" [PR comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3611773589)
  - 2026-07-20: Sid created this ticket to keep PR #1216 a pure extraction, and replied that `SharedNode` is "a lightweight listing of what a user sees for the nodes that are in shared space." [PR comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3613796080)
  - 2026-07-22: Michael on PR #1216: "eventually should be CrossAppNode contract, but that can be defered to the next project". [PR comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3632617180)
  - 2026-10-22: Sid decided this ticket waits for ENG-2091 and reads its type.

input.body:
Decision (Sid, 2026-10-23): this ticket becomes a sub-issue of ENG-2091. It lands after ENG-2091 adds the discovery function that returns `CrossAppNode`, and before ENG-2091 removes `SharedNode`, so the wrapper is deleted once instead of rewritten and then deleted. This refines the 2026-10-22 decision: the ticket still waits for ENG-2091's type.

Open, needs Marc-Antoine: whether `CrossAppNode` carries the author's database account id, which the import dialog uses for author names. It is one of the three fields in ENG-2091's open question.

History is in the description.

  * ISO strings (`created` / `lastModified`) → epoch numbers (`createdAt` / `modifiedAt`)
  * `directMetadata` (`Json`) → extracted `filePath: string | undefined`
* Michael on PR <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>: "`getPublishedNodesForGroups` is now redundant. It looks like the only thing it is doing is adding `filePath`, which doesn't warrant an entire wrapped function."
* <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> replaces `SharedNode` with `CrossAppNode`. It can't remove `SharedNode` while this wrapper, Obsidian's only reader of shared discovery, still uses it.

## Solution

* Remove the `getPublishedNodesForGroups` wrapper and the local `PublishedNode` type. Have `ImportNodesModal` (and the `ImportableNode` conversion path) read `CrossAppNode` directly, moving the `filePath`-from-`directMetadata` extraction to the single call site that needs it.

The wrapper is then deleted once, not rewritten and then deleted.

**Open decisions**

1. The import dialog shows author names by the author's database account id (`ImportNodesModal.tsx:130`, `:371-373`; `typeUtils.ts:92-97`). Does `CrossAppNode` carry that id, or does Obsidian look names up by the account's local id? This is one of the three fields in <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue>'s open question for Marc-Antoine.

* `getPublishedNodesForGroups` and the local `PublishedNode` type are gone.
